issue.title: Tabulator unable to be compiled by webpack

repository.name: survey-analytics
repository.description: Customizable JavaScript library to create interactive survey data dashboards and facilitate survey results analysis for your end-users.

issue.body:
Hi there!

Just wanted to report an error we encountered, while trying to test if we can use the analytics package in addition to the survey-js package as well :) It seems like the tabulator does not work, as we cannot import the CSS files for it. 

Our setup is a NextJS setup.* 

**Our package.json has these version-numbers:**
```
"@types/node": "^16.11.6",
"@types/react": "^17.0.34",
"babel-plugin-import": "^1.13.3",

"prettier": "2.4.1",

```

**Solution (not a working one)**
We can fix the error by removing the below line from the top of our Tabulator.tsx file (indicated with <-------):
```
import React, { useEffect, useMemo, useState } from 'react';
import * as Survey from 'survey-react';
import { Tabulator } from 'survey-analytics/survey.analytics.tabulator.js';

import 'survey-analytics/survey.analytics.tabulator.css'; <-------
import 'tabulator-tables/dist/css/tabulator.min.css';
```
 
However this also means that the styling on the component disappears, so it becomes a chaos without flexbox CSS applied to it, which renders it not usable in practice

**As an extra detail, a developer of ours managed to get the CSS to compile with Webpack if he used NextJS 11**
It uses an older webpack version. We believe the issue lies with the survey-analytics component's CSS not working with the newer Webpack versions. Unfortunately downgrading our NextJS server caused other issues with other components..

*NB. As a sidenote, this meant we also faced some other issues. this issues will likely be big entry barriers for other users as well - they were for us - which is why I mention these as well now :) Our solution could not be built with the Tabulator component referred for two other reason that we managed to fix: 
1. The analytics package did not work with SSR. We managed to fix this by wrapping the tabulator with: "export default dynamic(() => import('./SurveyAnalyticsTabulatorComponent'), { ssr: false });")
2. With the survey-analytics library referred, we could not built our nextJS solution due to some "can't resolve fs" error. We fixed this by adding: "config.resolve.fallback = { fs: false, path: false };" to our NextJS config.

body: Same - created my findings over here https://github.com/surveyjs/survey-analytics/issues/181 as it was the CSS files from this library I encountered the issues with :) Maybe the info I posted there can help troubleshooting :)
It seems like its any 12.x.x version. Reverting to 11.x.x versions made us able to deploy again to production, so we will follow that version for a while.
FWIW my error surfaced via `scss` from Bootstrap which was importing an `svg`

I think that this issue is related to one of this changes:
- update `mini-css-plugin` at [v2](https://github.com/webpack-contrib/mini-css-extract-plugin/releases/tag/v2.0.0) in #30617 
  This rule seems correct: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/eb1b125940fac4d34616ae3fd6e0e34165918dfb/packages/next/build/webpack/config/blocks/css/index.ts#L354-L367
- `resolve-url-loader` in #30743 (probably)

To investigate with next.js [v12.0.3-canary.2 changes](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/releases/tag/v12.0.3-canary.2).

FYI @sokra @ijjk @timneutkens
I can confirm it works on `12.0.3-canary.1` but not on `12.0.3-canary.2`

> FWIW my error surfaced via `scss` from Bootstrap which was importing an `svg`

Having this same issue with importing Bootstrap.
Confirm same problem `content: url("data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg...` in my `.scss` cause error.

12.0.3-canary.10, 12.0.3-canary.1, 12.0.3, 12.0.2, 12.0.1 are not working here because of this issue. Versions before 12.0.3 have problems building on docker because of https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/30713
We had to revert to 11.1.2.
